name: Guardian Initiate (Piety)
body:
Note Piety feats are intended for divine-classed followers of a specific deity. Each piety feat indicates which deity in question you must have selected as your patron deity. You cannot retrain or swap out a piety feat by any means, except as described below. Should you no longer meet any of the prerequisites of a piety feat, you lose all benefits of that piety feat (including spells added to your spell list or feat(s) gained from the piety feat). If you have lost access to a piety feat in this manner, you can either seek atonement (as determined by a powerful outsider sent by your deity) to regain the benefits and use of your piety feat or you may retrain it out for another feat that you meet the prerequisites for.

However, if you wish to retrain out a defunct and inaccessible piety feat for another piety feat granted by a new patron deity, you must wait at least 30 days and prove your worth (as determined by the GM) to the church of your new patron deity before you can select the piety feat associated with that deity.

You can possess multiple piety feats if they have the same specific patron deity listed in their prerequisites; otherwise, you cannot have more than one piety feat.

Prerequisite(s): 5 class levels in any one divine spellcasting class, Wis 15+, Cha 15+, and Deific Obedience ([this god]); you must have [this god] as your patron deity and your alignment must not be NE, CN, or CE (or must be within the alignment restriction of your divine spellcasting class that requires a patron deity).

Benefit: You may make a number of additional attacks of opportunity per round equal to your spellcasting ability modifier for the class you used to qualify for this piety feat at the time you gained this piety feat. You may also make attacks of opportunity while flat-footed (including if your weapon is sheathed, so long as you have Quick Draw or similar ability to draw your weapon as part of an attack of opportunity, such as a legendary samurai’s sheathed control). This feat counts as Combat Reflexes for all purposes and effects (including meeting feat prerequisites); this feat does not stack with Combat Reflexes for all purposes and effects.

If you already have Combat Reflexes when you gain this piety feat (or later gain Combat Reflexes while you have this piety feat), you automatically retrain Combat Reflexes, without spending time or money, for any one other feat as a bonus feat that you qualify for at the time you gained this piety feat. (Most worshippers of Tau typically select the Bodyguard feat in this manner.)

You also add the spells below at the spell level listed to the spell list of any and all divine spellcasting classes you possess that meet the prerequisites of this piety feat.

Adding these spells as spells known does not count against your spells known limit for any such divine spellcasting classes in this manner. If you possess the guardian domain, these spells are also considered domain spells for the guardian domain.

2nd-warning bell; 3rd-greater stunning barrier; 4th-protection from natural attacks, vigilante rest; 5th–stoneskin; 8th–protection from spells; 9th-greater mass ironward.

Normal: A character without this feat (or Combat Reflexes) can make only one attack of opportunity per round and can’t make attacks of opportunity while flatfooted.

Special: This feat does not allow a character to use any ability, feat, or talent more than once per round if that ability, feat, or talent requires an use (or more) of an attack of opportunity.
